source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Document the specific guidelines or requirements that the building failed to meet. This can include missing or malfunctioning smoke detectors, lack of fire extinguishers, blocked exits, evidence of improper storage of flammable materials, etc.
3. Record the exact locations within the building where the failures occurred. Take photos, if possible, to provide clear visual evidence of the issues.
4. Note any previous warnings or notices given to the property owner or manager regarding the fire safety violations.
5. Record the date and time of the inspection, and ensure the identity of the inspector or contractors performing the inspection is documented.
6. Describe any conversations or communications had with the building manager, owner, or other responsible parties regarding the failed checks. Include details on whether remedies were promised and by when.
7. Include information on any interactions with local fire departments or safety enforcement agencies, such as notices of violation issued by them.
8. Document any immediate actions or temporary remedies that you recommended
